### Pass signals directly to useQuery arguments in Solid Query

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/solid/quick-start.md

Signals and store values can be passed directly into function arguments, and Solid Query updates the query store automatically when the signal value changes. The example uses enabled() and todo() inside the useQuery options function.

```tsx
import {
  QueryClient,
  QueryClientProvider,
  useQuery,
} from '@tanstack/solid-query'
import { createSignal, For } from 'solid-js'

const queryClient = new QueryClient()

function Example() {
  const [enabled, setEnabled] = createSignal(false)
  const [todo, setTodo] = createSignal(0)

  // ✅ passing a signal directly is safe and observers update
  // automatically when the value of a signal changes
  const todosQuery = useQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todos'],
    queryFn: fetchTodos,
    enabled: enabled(),
  }))

  const todoDetailsQuery = useQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todo', todo()],
    queryFn: fetchTodo,
    enabled: todo() > 0,
  }))

  return (
    <div>
      <Switch>
        <Match when={todosQuery.isPending}>
          <p>Loading...</p>
        </Match>
        <Match when={todosQuery.isError}>
          <p>Error: {todosQuery.error.message}</p>
        </Match>
        <Match when={todosQuery.isSuccess}>
          <For each={todosQuery.data}>
            {(todo) => (
              <button onClick={() => setTodo(todo.id)}>{todo.title}</button>
            )}
          </For>
        </Match>
      </Switch>
      <button onClick={() => setEnabled(!enabled())}>Toggle enabled</button>
    </div>
  )
}

function App() {
  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <Example />
    </QueryClientProvider>
  )
}
```

### Basic Solid Query example with useQuery, ErrorBoundary, and Suspense

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/solid/overview.md

Basic Solid Query example that fetches GitHub stats for the TanStack Query repository. Uses useQuery with throwOnError and wraps the component in ErrorBoundary and Suspense to handle errors and loading states.

```tsx
import {
  useQuery,
  QueryClient,
  QueryClientProvider,
} from '@tanstack/solid-query'
import { ErrorBoundary, Suspense } from 'solid-js'

function App() {
  const repositoryQuery = useQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['TanStack Query'],
    queryFn: async () => {
      const result = await fetch('https://api.github.com/repos/TanStack/query')
      if (!result.ok) throw new Error('Failed to fetch data')
      return result.json()
    },
    staleTime: 5 * 60 * 1000, // 5 minutes
    throwOnError: true, // Throw an error if the query fails
  }))

  return (
    <div>
      <div>Static Content</div>
      {/* An error while fetching will be caught by the ErrorBoundary */}
      <ErrorBoundary fallback={<div>Something went wrong!</div>}>
        {/* Suspense will trigger a loading state while the data is being fetched */}
        <Suspense fallback={<div>Loading...</div>}>
          {/* 
            The `data` property on a query is a SolidJS resource  
            so it will work with Suspense and transitions out of the box! 
          */}
          <div>{repositoryQuery.data?.updated_at}</div>
        </Suspense>
      </ErrorBoundary>
    </div>
  )
}

const root = document.getElementById('root')
const client = new QueryClient()

render(
  () => (
    <QueryClientProvider client={client}>
      <App />
    </QueryClientProvider>
  ),
  root!,
)
```

### Set up QueryClientProvider and useQuery in SolidJS

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/solid/quick-start.md

Create a QueryClient and wrap the app in QueryClientProvider, then fetch todos with useQuery and render pending, error, and success states using Solid's Switch/Match/For.

```tsx
import {
  QueryClient,
  QueryClientProvider,
  useQuery,
} from '@tanstack/solid-query'
import { Switch, Match, For } from 'solid-js'

const queryClient = new QueryClient()

function Example() {
  const query = useQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todos'],
    queryFn: fetchTodos,
  }))

  return (
    <div>
      <Switch>
        <Match when={query.isPending}>
          <p>Loading...</p>
        </Match>
        <Match when={query.isError}>
          <p>Error: {query.error.message}</p>
        </Match>
        <Match when={query.isSuccess}>
          <For each={query.data}>{(todo) => <p>{todo.title}</p>}</For>
        </Match>
      </Switch>
    </div>
  )
}

function App() {
  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <Example />
    </QueryClientProvider>
  )
}
```

### Use useQuery with <script setup>

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/vue/installation.md

All documentation examples use the <script setup> syntax. Vue 2 users can use it via the unplugin-vue2-script-setup plugin; otherwise translate to normal Composition API by moving code into setup() and returning template values.

```vue
<script setup>
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

const { isPending, isFetching, isError, data, error } = useQuery({
  queryKey: ['todos'],
  queryFn: getTodos,
})
</script>

<template>...</template>
```

### useInfiniteQuery with initialData example

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/preact/reference/functions/useInfiniteQuery.md

Example of useInfiniteQuery with initialData, ensuring data is never undefined even if a refetch fails. The list stays visible alongside any error.

```tsx
import { useInfiniteQuery } from '@tanstack/preact-query'

function Projects() {
  // `data` is never `undefined`, thanks to `initialData` — even if a refetch fails, so the
  // list stays visible alongside the error.
  const { data, isError, error } = useInfiniteQuery({
    queryKey: ['projects'],
    queryFn: ({ pageParam }) => fetchProjects(pageParam),
    initialPageParam: 0,
    getNextPageParam: (lastPage) => lastPage.nextId,
    initialData: { pages: [], pageParams: [] },
  })

  return (
    <div>
      {isError ? <span>Error: {error.message}</span> : null}
      <ul>
        {data.pages.map((page) => page.projects.map((p) => <li key={p.id}>{p.name}</li>))}
      </ul>
    </div>
  )
}
```

  queryKey: ['todos'],

  initialData: [],

### Use useQueryClient in a Vue component

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/vue/reference/functions/useQueryClient.md

Use useQueryClient inside a Vue component's setup to access the installed QueryClient and invalidate queries. The id parameter is only needed when multiple QueryClients are installed in the same app.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

const queryClient = useQueryClient()

function invalidate() {
  queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] })
}
</script>
```

--------------------------------

### Quick Start with createQueryController and QueryClientProvider

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/packages/lit-query/README.md

Sets up a QueryClient, provides it via QueryClientProvider, and uses createQueryController to fetch and render users in a LitElement.

```ts
import {
  QueryClient,
  QueryClientProvider,
  createQueryController,
} from '@tanstack/lit-query'
import { LitElement, html } from 'lit'

const client = new QueryClient({
  defaultOptions: { queries: { retry: false } },
})

class AppProvider extends QueryClientProvider {
  constructor() {
    super()
    this.client = client
  }
}
customElements.define('app-provider', AppProvider)

class UsersView extends LitElement {
  private readonly users = createQueryController(this, {
    queryKey: ['users'],
    queryFn: async () => {
      const response = await fetch('/api/users')
      return response.json() as Promise<Array<{ id: string; name: string }>>
    },
  })

  render() {
    const query = this.users()
    if (query.isPending) return html`Loading...`
    if (query.isError) return html`Error`
    return html`<ul>
      ${query.data?.map((u) => html`<li>${u.name}</li>`)}
    </ul>`
  }
}
customElements.define('users-view', UsersView)
```

### Basic useQuery with Solid

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/solid/reference/functions/useQuery.md

Use this basic useQuery example to fetch and render a list of posts with loading, error, and success states.

```tsx
import { For, Match, Switch } from 'solid-js'
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/solid-query'

function Posts() {
  const postsQuery = useQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['posts'],
    queryFn: fetchPosts,
  }))

  return (
    <Switch>
      <Match when={postsQuery.isPending}>Loading...</Match>
      <Match when={postsQuery.isError}>Error: {postsQuery.error.message}</Match>
      <Match when={postsQuery.isSuccess}>
        <ul>
          <For each={postsQuery.data}>{(post) => <li>{post.title}</li>}</For>
        </ul>
        <div>{postsQuery.isFetching ? 'Background Updating...' : ' '}</div>
      </Match>
    </Switch>
  )
}
```

--------------------------------

### getQueryCache() example

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/reference/classes/QueryClient.md

Creates a QueryClient, gets its QueryCache, and finds all queries with key ['posts'].

```ts
import { QueryClient } from '@tanstack/query-core'

const queryClient = new QueryClient()
const queryCache = queryClient.getQueryCache()
const queries = queryCache.findAll({ queryKey: ['posts'] })
```

--------------------------------

### Use mutateAsync to get a promise from a mutation

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/react/guides/mutations.md

Use mutateAsync instead of mutate to get a promise that resolves on success or throws on error. This allows composing side effects with try/catch/finally.

```tsx
const mutation = useMutation({ mutationFn: addTodo })

try {
  const todo = await mutation.mutateAsync(todo)
  console.log(todo)
} catch (error) {
  console.error(error)
} finally {
  console.log('done')
}
```

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/lit/reference/classes/InfiniteQueryObserver.md

Example of using fetchOptimistic to prefetch a query and log the result data.

```ts
const result = await observer.fetchOptimistic({
  queryKey: ['posts', 2],
  queryFn: () => fetchPost(2),
})
console.log(result.data)
```

### setOptions() example

```ts

observer.setOptions({ queryKey: ['posts', 2], queryFn: () => fetchPost(2) })

### useQueryClient function signature

Retrieves the QueryClient installed by VueQueryPlugin via Vue's inject. Must be called inside setup() or another function that supports an injection context. Throws if called outside an injection context or if no QueryClient was installed via VueQueryPlugin.

function useQueryClient(id?: string): QueryClient;

### Invalidate queries by key prefix

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/guides/query-invalidation.md

Invalidates matching queries starting with the specified queryKey prefix. In this example, both the base 'todos' and the parameterized 'todos' queries are invalidated.

```ts
import { injectQuery, QueryClient } from '@tanstack/angular-query-experimental'

class QueryInvalidationExample {
  readonly queryClient = inject(QueryClient)

  invalidateQueries() {
    this.queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] })
  }

  // Both queries below will be invalidated
  todoListQuery = injectQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todos'],
    queryFn: fetchTodoList,
  }))
  todoListQuery = injectQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todos', { page: 1 }],
    queryFn: fetchTodoList,
  }))
}
```

### Set up QueryClientProvider and fetch data with createQuery

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/svelte/overview.md

Configure QueryClientProvider at the project root and consume createQuery inside child components. Arguments to createQuery must be wrapped in a function to maintain reactivity in Svelte.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/svelte-query'
  import Example from './lib/Example.svelte'

  const queryClient = new QueryClient()
</script>

<QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
  <Example />
</QueryClientProvider>
```

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { createQuery } from '@tanstack/svelte-query'

  const query = createQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todos'],
    queryFn: () => fetchTodos(),
  }))
</script>

<div>
  {#if query.isPending}
    <p>Loading...</p>
  {:else if query.isError}
    <p>Error: {query.error.message}</p>
  {:else if query.isSuccess}
    {#each query.data as todo}
      <p>{todo.title}</p>
    {/each}
  {/if}
</div>
```

### Set up QueryClientProvider with useQuery and useMutation in Preact

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/preact/quick-start.md

Creates a QueryClient and provides it to the app via QueryClientProvider. Uses useQuery to fetch todos and useMutation to add a todo, invalidating the ['todos'] query on success.

```tsx
import {
  useQuery,
  useMutation,
  useQueryClient,
  QueryClient,
  QueryClientProvider,
} from '@tanstack/preact-query'
import { render } from 'preact'
import { getTodos, postTodo } from '../my-api'

// Create a client
const queryClient = new QueryClient()

function App() {
  return (
    // Provide the client to your App
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <Todos />
    </QueryClientProvider>
  )
}

function Todos() {
  // Access the client
  const queryClient = useQueryClient()

  // Queries
  const query = useQuery({ queryKey: ['todos'], queryFn: getTodos })

  // Mutations
  const mutation = useMutation({
    mutationFn: postTodo,
    onSuccess: () => {
      // Invalidate and refetch
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] })
    },
  })

  return (
    <div>
      <ul>
        {query.data?.map((todo) => (
          <li key={todo.id}>{todo.title}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>

      <button
        onClick={() => {
          mutation.mutate({
            id: Date.now(),
            title: 'Do Laundry',
          })
        }}
      >
        Add Todo
      </button>
    </div>
  )
}

render(<App />, document.getElementById('root'))
```

### useQueryClient

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/vue/reference/functions/useQueryClient.md

Retrieves the QueryClient installed by VueQueryPlugin, via Vue's inject. Must be called inside setup() or another function that supports an injection context.

```APIDOC
## useQueryClient

### Description
Retrieves the `QueryClient` installed by `VueQueryPlugin`, via Vue's `inject`. Must be called inside `setup()` or another function that supports an injection context.

### Signature
```ts
function useQueryClient(id?: string): QueryClient;
```

### Parameters
- **id?** (`string`) - Optional - The `queryClientKey` passed to `VueQueryPlugin` — only needed when multiple `QueryClient`s are installed in the same app. Defaults to `''`.

### Returns
`QueryClient` - The installed `QueryClient`.

### Throws
If called outside an injection context, or if no `QueryClient` was installed via `VueQueryPlugin`.

### Example
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

const queryClient = useQueryClient()

function invalidate() {
  queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] })
}
</script>
```
```

### Request Waterfall Example with Article and Comments

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/react/guides/prefetching.md

Shows a request waterfall where Comments query starts only after Article query resolves. Use this to understand the problem before applying prefetching.

```tsx
function Article({ id }) {
  const { data: articleData, isPending } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['article', id],
    queryFn: getArticleById,
  })

  if (isPending) {
    return 'Loading article...'
  }

  return (
    <>
      <ArticleHeader articleData={articleData} />
      <ArticleBody articleData={articleData} />
      <Comments id={id} />
    </>
  )
}

function Comments({ id }) {
  const { data, isPending } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['article-comments', id],
    queryFn: getArticleCommentsById,
  })

  ...
}
```

### Use mutateAsync with Promise.all for multiple mutations

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/react/reference/functions/useMutation.md

Callbacks passed to mutate only fire for the last call; use mutateAsync to get a promise per call and await all with Promise.all. This example adds multiple todos and handles errors.

```tsx
import { useMutation, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query'

function AddTodos() {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient()

  const addMutation = useMutation({
    mutationFn: addTodo,
    onSuccess: () => queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] }),
  })

  async function handleAddAll(todos: Array<string>) {
    try {
      await Promise.all(todos.map((todo) => addMutation.mutateAsync(todo)))
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Failed to add todos:', error)
    }
  }

  return (
    <button onClick={() => handleAddAll(['Todo 1', 'Todo 2', 'Todo 3'])}>
      Add all
    </button>
  )
}
```

--------------------------------

### Conditional lazy loading causing double request waterfall

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/react/guides/prefetching.md

Example from the Performance & Request Waterfalls guide showing a double request waterfall when GraphFeedItem is lazy loaded and its data is fetched only after rendering.

```tsx
// This lazy loads the GraphFeedItem component, meaning
// it won't start loading until something renders it
const GraphFeedItem = React.lazy(() => import('./GraphFeedItem'))

function Feed() {
  const { data, isPending } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['feed'],
    queryFn: getFeed,
  })

  if (isPending) {
    return 'Loading feed...'
  }

  return (
    <>
      {data.map((feedItem) => {
        if (feedItem.type === 'GRAPH') {
          return <GraphFeedItem key={feedItem.id} feedItem={feedItem} />
        }

        return <StandardFeedItem key={feedItem.id} feedItem={feedItem} />
      })}
    </>
  )
}

// GraphFeedItem.tsx
function GraphFeedItem({ feedItem }) {
  const { data, isPending } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['graph', feedItem.id],
    queryFn: getGraphDataById,
  })

  ...
}
```

### Augment Register to set defaultError with AxiosError

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/reference/interfaces/Register.md

Augment the installed adapter module's Register interface to override the default error type. This example uses the React adapter; augmenting @tanstack/query-core instead covers every adapter at once.

```ts
// Use the module you installed — here, the React adapter.
declare module '@tanstack/react-query' {
  interface Register {
    defaultError: AxiosError
  }
}
```

### Basic TanStack Query example with injectQuery in Angular

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/overview.md

Use this basic example to fetch GitHub stats for the TanStack Query repository using injectQuery and HttpClient. It shows pending, error, and success states in the template.

```angular-ts
import { HttpClient } from '@angular/common/http'
import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, inject } from '@angular/core'
import { injectQuery } from '@tanstack/angular-query-experimental'
import { lastValueFrom } from 'rxjs'

@Component({
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  selector: 'simple-example',
  template: `
    @if (repoDataQuery.isPending()) {
      Loading...
    }
    @if (repoDataQuery.isError()) {
      An error has occurred: {{ repoDataQuery.error().message }}
    }
    @if (repoDataQuery.data(); as data) {
      <h1>{{ data.name }}</h1>
      <p>{{ data.description }}</p>
      <strong>👀 {{ data.subscribers_count }}</strong>
      <strong>✨ {{ data.stargazers_count }}</strong>
      <strong>🍴 {{ data.forks_count }}</strong>
    }
  `,
})
export class SimpleExampleComponent {
  readonly http = inject(HttpClient)

  readonly repoDataQuery = injectQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['repoData'],
    queryFn: () =>
      lastValueFrom(
        this.http.get<Repo>('https://api.github.com/repos/TanStack/query'),
      ),
  }))
}

interface Repo {
  name: string
  description: string
  subscribers_count: number
  stargazers_count: number
  forks_count: number
}

```

--------------------------------

### Nuxt 3 Vue Query plugin setup (vue-query.ts)

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/vue/guides/ssr.md

Create this file in your Nuxt 3 plugins directory to set up Vue Query with SSR. It configures a QueryClient, installs the plugin, and dehydrates/hydrates the query state on server and client.

```ts
import {
  VueQueryPlugin,
  QueryClient,
  hydrate,
  dehydrate,
} from '@tanstack/vue-query'
// Nuxt 3 app aliases
import { defineNuxtPlugin, useState } from '#imports'
import type {
  DehydratedState,
  VueQueryPluginOptions,
} from '@tanstack/vue-query'

export default defineNuxtPlugin((nuxt) => {
  const vueQueryState = useState<DehydratedState | null>('vue-query')

  // Modify your Vue Query global settings here
  const queryClient = new QueryClient({
    defaultOptions: { queries: { staleTime: 5 * 1000 } },
  })
  const options: VueQueryPluginOptions = { queryClient }

  nuxt.vueApp.use(VueQueryPlugin, options)

  if (import.meta.server) {
    nuxt.hooks.hook('app:rendered', () => {
      vueQueryState.value = dehydrate(queryClient)
    })
  }

  if (import.meta.client && vueQueryState.value !== null) {
    hydrate(queryClient, vueQueryState.value)
  }
})
```

--------------------------------

### setEventListener() method signature and example

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/reference/interfaces/FocusManager.md

`setEventListener` can be used to set a custom event listener that will be used to determine the focus state. The provided `setup` function receives a `setFocused` callback: call it with a `boolean` to manually set the focus state, or with no arguments to re-evaluate the current focus state and notify subscribers.

```ts
setEventListener(setup: SetupFn): void;
```

```ts
import { focusManager } from '@tanstack/query-core'

focusManager.setEventListener((handleFocus) => {
  const listener = () => handleFocus()
  // Listen to visibilitychange
  if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.addEventListener) {
    window.addEventListener('visibilitychange', listener, false)
  }

  return () => {
    // Be sure to unsubscribe if a new handler is set
    window.removeEventListener('visibilitychange', listener)
  }
})
```

--------------------------------

### Set up QueryClientProvider with per-request QueryClient in SolidStart

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/solid/guides/ssr.md

Create the QueryClient inside the App component so SolidStart makes a fresh one per request, preventing cached data from being shared between users. The Suspense boundary is required because useQuery suspends while pending on both server and client.

```tsx
// src/app.tsx
import { MetaProvider, Title } from '@solidjs/meta'
import { Router } from '@solidjs/router'
import { FileRoutes } from '@solidjs/start/router'
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/solid-query'
import { Suspense } from 'solid-js'

export default function App() {
  // Constructing the QueryClient inside the component (rather than at module
  // scope) means SolidStart creates a fresh one for every request, so data
  // is never shared between users.
  const queryClient = new QueryClient({
    defaultOptions: {
      queries: {
        // staleTime governs refetches from later triggers (a new mount, window
        // focus, and so on) — see Solid Query's hydration model above for why
        // the very first mount after SSR doesn't need it to skip a refetch.
        staleTime: 5 * 1000,
      },
    },
  })

  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <Router
        root={(props) => (
          <MetaProvider>
            <Title>My App</Title>
            <Suspense>{props.children}</Suspense>
          </MetaProvider>
        )}
      >
        <FileRoutes />
      </Router>
    </QueryClientProvider>
  )
}
```

--------------------------------

### createInfiniteQueryController

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/lit/reference/functions/createInfiniteQueryController.md

Creates a Lit reactive controller that subscribes the host to an infinite query. The returned accessor is callable and also exposes current, refetch, fetchNextPage, fetchPreviousPage, and destroy. When options is a function, it is re-read during host updates so query keys and options can follow reactive host state. If queryClient is omitted, the controller resolves the client from the nearest connected QueryClientProvider.

```APIDOC
## createInfiniteQueryController

### Description

Creates a Lit reactive controller that subscribes the host to an infinite query.

### Signature

```ts
function createInfiniteQueryController<
  TQueryFnData = unknown,
  TError = Error,
  TData = InfiniteData<TQueryFnData, unknown>,
  TQueryKey extends readonly unknown[] = readonly unknown[],
  TPageParam = unknown
>(
  host: ReactiveControllerHost,
  options: Accessor<
    CreateInfiniteQueryOptions<TQueryFnData, TError, TData, TQueryKey, TPageParam>
  >,
  queryClient?: QueryClient
): InfiniteQueryResultAccessor<TData, TError>;
```

### Type Parameters

- **TQueryFnData** = `unknown`
- **TError** = `Error`
- **TData** = `InfiniteData<TQueryFnData, unknown>`
- **TQueryKey** extends `readonly unknown[]` = `readonly unknown[]`
- **TPageParam** = `unknown`

### Parameters

- **host** (`ReactiveControllerHost`) - The Lit reactive controller host that owns the infinite query subscription.
- **options** (`Accessor<CreateInfiniteQueryOptions<TQueryFnData, TError, TData, TQueryKey, TPageParam>>`) - Infinite query observer options, or a getter that returns options.
- **queryClient?** (`QueryClient`) - Optional explicit query client. Provide this for controllers that should not resolve a client from Lit context.

### Returns

`InfiniteQueryResultAccessor<TData, TError>` - An accessor for the latest infinite query result with page helper methods.

### Example

```ts
import { LitElement, html } from 'lit'
import { createInfiniteQueryController } from '@tanstack/lit-query'

class ProjectsView extends LitElement {
  private readonly projects = createInfiniteQueryController(this, {
    queryKey: ['projects'],
    queryFn: ({ pageParam }) => fetchProjects(pageParam),
    initialPageParam: 0,
    getNextPageParam: (lastPage) => lastPage.nextCursor,
  })

  render() {
    const query = this.projects()

    return html`
      <button ?disabled=${!query.hasNextPage} @click=${() => this.projects.fetchNextPage()}>
        Load more
      </button>
    `
  }
}
```
```

--------------------------------

### Configure useMutation with a scope id to serialize mutations

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/react/guides/mutations.md

By default all mutations run in parallel, even repeated calls to the same mutation. Giving mutations the same scope.id runs them in serial: a triggered mutation starts in isPaused: true if another mutation for that scope is in progress, is queued, and resumes automatically when its turn comes.

```tsx
const mutation = useMutation({
  mutationFn: addTodo,
  scope: {
    id: 'todo',
  },
})
```

### Full SSR example with preact-render-to-string

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/preact/guides/ssr.md

Server entry point prefetches queries with a prefetching client, dehydrates the state, hydrates a separate render client, and renders to string. Client entry point hydrates the dehydrated state into a new query client and wraps the tree with HydrationBoundary. Use both together for SSR with Preact.

```tsx
import {
  QueryCache,
  QueryClient,
  QueryClientProvider,
  dehydrate,
  hydrate,
  noop,
} from '@tanstack/preact-query'
import { renderToString } from 'preact-render-to-string'

function makeQueryClient() {
  return new QueryClient({
    queryCache: new QueryCache(),
    defaultOptions: {
      queries: {
        // With SSR, we usually want to set some default staleTime
        // above 0 to avoid refetching immediately on the client
        staleTime: 60 * 1000,
      },
    },
  })
}

export async function render(url) {
  // The prefetching client: only used to fetch and dehydrate
  const prefetchClient = makeQueryClient()

  await prefetchClient
    .query({
      queryKey: ['posts'],
      queryFn: getPosts,
    })
    .catch(noop)

  const dehydratedState = dehydrate(prefetchClient)

  // The render client: hydrated with the same state, used for renderToString
  const renderClient = makeQueryClient()
  hydrate(renderClient, dehydratedState)

  const appHtml = renderToString(
    <QueryClientProvider client={renderClient}>
      <App />
    </QueryClientProvider>,
  )

  // Embed both the markup and the dehydrated state in the html you send down.
  // Use a safe serializer here (see Serialization below), NOT JSON.stringify,
  // since raw JSON.stringify output can break out of the <script> tag:
  // e.g. `<div id="app">${appHtml}</div><script>window.__DEHYDRATED_STATE__ = ${serialize(dehydratedState)}</script>`
  return { appHtml, dehydratedState }
}
```

```tsx
import {
  HydrationBoundary,
  QueryClient,
  QueryClientProvider,
} from '@tanstack/preact-query'
import { hydrate as preactHydrate } from 'preact'
import { useState } from 'preact/hooks'

function makeQueryClient() {
  return new QueryClient({
    defaultOptions: {
      queries: {
        // With SSR, we usually want to set some default staleTime
        // above 0 to avoid refetching immediately on the client
        staleTime: 60 * 1000,
      },
    },
  })
}

function App({ dehydratedState }) {
  const [queryClient] = useState(() => makeQueryClient())

  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <HydrationBoundary state={dehydratedState}>
        <Posts />
      </HydrationBoundary>
    </QueryClientProvider>
  )
}

// Read back and deserialize whatever you embedded on the server,
// e.g. `window.__DEHYDRATED_STATE__`
preactHydrate(
  <App dehydratedState={window.__DEHYDRATED_STATE__} />,
  document.getElementById('app'),
)
```

### Lit Query quick start with createQueryController and createMutationController

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/lit/quick-start.md

Shows the three core Lit Query concepts: queries, mutations, and query invalidation. The controllers are created with `this` because a `LitElement` is a `ReactiveControllerHost`; Lit Query uses the host lifecycle to subscribe, request updates, and clean up when the element disconnects. Mount the provider around your component as shown in the HTML snippet.

```ts
import {
  QueryClient,
  QueryClientProvider,
  createMutationController,
  createQueryController,
} from '@tanstack/lit-query'
import { LitElement, html } from 'lit'
import { addTodo, getTodos } from './api'

const queryClient = new QueryClient()

class AppQueryProvider extends QueryClientProvider {
  constructor() {
    super()
    this.client = queryClient
  }
}

customElements.define('app-query-provider', AppQueryProvider)

class TodosView extends LitElement {
  private readonly todos = createQueryController(this, {
    queryKey: ['todos'],
    queryFn: getTodos,
  })

  private readonly createTodo = createMutationController(this, {
    mutationFn: addTodo,
    onSuccess: async () => {
      await queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] })
    },
  })

  render() {
    const query = this.todos()
    const mutation = this.createTodo()

    if (query.isPending) return html`Loading...`
    if (query.isError) return html`Error: ${query.error.message}`

    return html`
      <ul>
        ${query.data.map((todo) => html`<li>${todo.title}</li>`)}
      </ul>

      <button
        ?disabled=${mutation.isPending}
        @click=${() => this.createTodo.mutate({ title: 'Write Lit docs' })}
      >
        Add Todo
      </button>
    `
  }
}

customElements.define('todos-view', TodosView)
```

```html
<app-query-provider>
  <todos-view></todos-view>
</app-query-provider>
```

### useIsMutating example with mutationKey filter

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/preact/reference/functions/useIsMutating.md

Example usage of useIsMutating to show a loading indicator when mutations with the 'posts' mutationKey are pending. Returns a number of pending mutations.

```tsx
import { useIsMutating } from '@tanstack/preact-query'

function PostsMutatingIndicator() {
  // How many mutations matching the posts prefix are in progress?
  const isMutatingPosts = useIsMutating({ mutationKey: ['posts'] })

  return isMutatingPosts ? <span>Saving posts...</span> : null
}
```

### Pass options as a function to useQuery in Solid Query

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/solid/quick-start.md

Solid Query primitives like useQuery, useMutation, and useIsFetching take arguments as functions so they can be tracked in a reactive scope. The React-style object argument is shown as incorrect.

```tsx
// ❌ react version
useQuery({
  queryKey: ['todos', todo],
  queryFn: fetchTodos,
})

// ✅ solid version
useQuery(() => ({
  queryKey: ['todos', todo],
  queryFn: fetchTodos,
}))
```

### Using useQuery in a component with prefetched and client-only queries

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/preact/guides/ssr.md

Shows how to use useQuery inside a component. The first query is prefetched on the server and available immediately; the second is not prefetched and will fetch on the client. Both patterns can be mixed.

```tsx
function Posts() {
  // This useQuery could just as well happen in some deeper child to <App>,
  // data will be available immediately either way
  const { data } = useQuery({ queryKey: ['posts'], queryFn: getPosts })

  // This query was not prefetched on the server and will not start
  // fetching until on the client, both patterns are fine to mix
  const { data: commentsData } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['posts-comments'],
    queryFn: getComments,
  })

  // ...
}
```

### Set up QueryClientProvider in Svelte

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/svelte/quick-start.md

Wrap your app with QueryClientProvider and pass a QueryClient instance to provide the query client to all components.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/svelte-query'
  import Example from './lib/Example.svelte'

  const queryClient = new QueryClient()
</script>

<QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
  <Example />
</QueryClientProvider>
```

--------------------------------

### Set up QueryClientProvider for Server Components in Next.js

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/react/guides/advanced-ssr.md

Create a QueryClient and wrap the app in QueryClientProvider for Server Components. In Next.js, split into app/providers.tsx and app/layout.tsx. The providers file must have 'use client' at the top.

```tsx
// In Next.js, this file would be called: app/providers.tsx
'use client'

// Since QueryClientProvider relies on useContext under the hood, we have to put 'use client' on top
import {
  environmentManager,
  QueryClient,
  QueryClientProvider,
} from '@tanstack/react-query'

function makeQueryClient() {
  return new QueryClient({
    defaultOptions: {
      queries: {
        // With SSR, we usually want to set some default staleTime
        // above 0 to avoid refetching immediately on the client
        staleTime: 60 * 1000,
      },
    },
  })
}

let browserQueryClient: QueryClient | undefined = undefined

function getQueryClient() {
  if (environmentManager.isServer()) {
    // Server: always make a new query client
    return makeQueryClient()
  } else {
    // Browser: make a new query client if we don't already have one
    // This is very important, so we don't re-make a new client if React
    // suspends during the initial render. This may not be needed if we
    // have a suspense boundary BELOW the creation of the query client
    if (!browserQueryClient) browserQueryClient = makeQueryClient()
    return browserQueryClient
  }
}

export default function Providers({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  // NOTE: Avoid useState when initializing the query client if you don't
  //       have a suspense boundary between this and the code that may
  //       suspend because React will throw away the client on the initial
  //       render if it suspends and there is no boundary
  const queryClient = getQueryClient()

  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>{children}</QueryClientProvider>
  )
}
```

```tsx
// In Next.js, this file would be called: app/layout.tsx
import Providers from './providers'

export default function RootLayout({
  children,
}: {
  children: React.ReactNode
}) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <head />
      <body>
        <Providers>{children}</Providers>
      </body>
    </html>
  )
}
```
